_comment: Tier-2 for fourc::structural_mechanics#12 — NUE is validated against the half-open interval [-1, 0.5), so the incompressible limit NUE: 0.5 is REFUSED at parse rather than merely ill-conditioned. Six arms of one Statics HEX8 deck, KINEM linear, the material the only change, run 2026-08-06 against 4C 2026.2.0-dev (git 89519cf) at /home/alexander/4C/build/4C. Observed: NUE 0.3 and NUE 0.4999 both exit 0 with 'processor 0 finished normally', so near-incompressible behaviour is reachable by backing off the limit; NUE 0.5 and NUE 0.6 both exit 1 with "Candidate parameter 'NUE' does not pass validation: in_range[-1,0.5)" inside the "Failed to match specification in section 'MATERIALS'" report from global_data/4C_global_data_read.cpp, and nothing is assembled (NUE_0_5_REACHED_FILL_COMPLETE=0). The two ends of the interval are asserted separately because that is what 'half-open' means in practice: NUE -1.000001 is rejected the same way, while NUE -1.0 is ACCEPTED by the validator (NUE_MINUS_1_VALIDATION_COMPLAINTS=0, NUE_MINUS_1_REACHED_FILL_COMPLETE=2) and is then killed by SIGFPE with shell status 136 — passing validation is not the same as being a usable material.
expect_in_output: Candidate parameter 'NUE' does not pass validation: in_range[-1,0.5)
Failed to match specification in section 'MATERIALS'

_mutation.note: remove the pathology: back the incompressible arm off the limit. The validation rejection disappears and EXIT_NUE_0_5 becomes 0, so the fixture must go red.
remove the pathology from the out-of-range arm too. EXIT_NUE_0_6 becomes 0, so the fixture must go red.
remove the pathology from the lower-end arm: move it inside the interval. The SIGFPE disappears and EXIT_NUE_MINUS_1 becomes 0, so the fixture must go red.
